claims.text: The anomalous strain-rate insensitivity of yield in single-crystal FeNiCrMn is driven by athermal screw-dislocation glide.
The relevant screw dislocations glide on {110} planes along ⟨111⟩ directions.
High Peierls stress creates athermal barriers that dominate over thermal activation.
The FeNiCrMn initial state is FCC or metastable FCC/BCC dual phase.
The initial crystal is free of significant pre-existing dislocation networks.
The selected crystal orientation maximizes resolved shear stress on {110}⟨111⟩ slip systems.
Above the Peierls stress, screw dislocations can exhibit viscous, non-thermally activated motion.
Yield onset in FeNiCrMn is governed by athermal overcoming of Peierls barriers by screw dislocations.
Lattice friction rather than thermal fluctuations determines the stress required to initiate slip.
Yield strength will remain nearly constant from 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^-1 s^-1 over 77–600 K.
Post-yield flow will exhibit intermittent wild plastic bursts or avalanches characteristic of athermal slip.
The avalanche-size distribution will shift from power-law to exponential as temperature decreases.
Traditional FCC metals such as pure Ni or Fe-Ni alloys exhibit a strong positive yield-strength dependence on strain rate because glide and cross-slip are thermally activated.
The mechanism requires BCC character or an FCC state with stacking-fault energetics that impede screw motion.
The mechanism fails in a purely soft FCC state with low stacking-fault energy where thermal activation dominates.
Tensile loading can produce a BCC-to-FCC phase transition in Ti68Nb7Ta3Zr4Mo18.
A ⟨123⟩ loading orientation maximizes screw-dislocation activity in FeNiCrMn.
A yield-stress increase greater than 5% per decade of strain rate would falsify athermal screw-dislocation dominance.
Persistence of a scale-free avalanche distribution at low temperature without an exponential shift would falsify the hypothesis.
In-situ diffraction can be used during loading to monitor whether phase transformation accompanies the onset of plasticity.

contradictions.description: The initial state permits a purely FCC crystal, but the asserted {110}⟨111⟩ screw-slip/Peierls mechanism is framed as requiring BCC character or an otherwise unconfirmed high-barrier FCC state.
